subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Batteries: Storing Electrons Chemically
description: A quick, practical guide to Batteries: Storing Electrons Chemically.

hook.text: A lithium-ion battery stores energy in chemical bonds. Charging forces lithium ions one way; discharging sends them back.

buildup.text: Two electrodes — an anode and a cathode — sit in an electrolyte. Ions shuttle between them carrying charge.

discovery.text: John Goodenough invented the lithium cobalt oxide cathode in 1980. He received the Nobel Prize in 2019 — at age 97.

twist.text: Lithium-ion batteries degrade with every cycle. After 1,000 charges, capacity drops to about 80% of original.

climax.text: Solid-state batteries replace liquid electrolyte with a solid. They promise double the energy density and no fire risk.

punchline.text: Chemistry stores electricity. Ions shuttle back and forth. Rechargeable.

quiz.question: What advantage do solid-state batteries promise over lithium-ion?
options: They cost half as much to manufacture at scale
They offer double the energy density with no fire risk
They never degrade regardless of the number of charge cycles
